item.title: Clinical AI and the Human-in-the-Loop Assumption: Four Questions Still Unanswered
item.description:
“Keep a human in the loop” has become the default answer to nearly every concern about AI in healthcare. If a clinician reviews the output, the reasoning goes, the patient is protected.

That reasoning rests on an assumption that is rarely tested: that the clinician in the loop is actually exercising judgment. A person can be formally part of a workflow and still have little real influence over its outcome. As AI tools spread into diagnosis, prescribing, monitoring, and documentation, the distance between those two situations is becoming one of the central safety questions in digital health.

item.title: A Native Bangla Chain-of-Thought Dataset: Filling a Foundational Gap in Language AI
item.description:
There is a category of problem in AI development that money alone cannot solve quickly.

You can fund compute. You can hire engineers. You can license existing datasets. But you cannot purchase native deliberative prose in a language where that genre of writing barely exists as a written form. That is the situation with Bangla and chain-of-thought reasoning data.

This article explains why that gap exists, why it matters, and what an open community dataset can do about it.
